role: independent revised scheduler static review and bounded synthetic tests; no owner integration claim
status: previous two scheduler blockers addressed; no additional snapshot leak identified in the reviewed module; integration unqualified

prior_findings_resolution.analysis: Phase functions now execute via a module-captured Reflect.apply with undefined receiver; frozen snapshot routing is never passed as receiver or argument. Test covers ordinary strict functions and an attempted this.final assignment; final counter proves the intended predicate ran.

Async/generator function kinds and proxy functions are rejected at graph capture; every executed local predicate must return exactly undefined. Test covers async/generator, a resolved Promise, a thenable object, generator object and booleans; final counter proves later final was not invoked.

static_observations: Dependency/root graph is captured from own data descriptors on plain non-Proxy objects and dense arrays; postorder identity dedup checks cycles; later root/node/dependency descriptor/value changes are checked before and after a successful call.
Each invocation reruns preflight for all captured nodes, then consume, then final; there is no source/owner/result cache. During execution no mutable snapshot is exposed via predicate receiver.
A caught nested reentrant rejection permits the outer operation to continue by design; its real final pass still runs. Uncaught nested failure clears running in finally, allowing a later clean call.

The exact-undefined protocol fails closed if a synchronous function returns a rejected Promise, but this test uses Promise.resolve rather than Promise.reject; an unhandled rejection from a bad adapter is a possible process-level failure and needs integration handling. Do not reinterpret a rejected adapter as a successful guard.

Metadata restored entirely before final is not itself detected by endpoint comparison. Captured routing prevents redirection, but real owner predicates must independently use isolated judgments and recheck meaningful live metadata.

bounded_test.scope: synthetic scheduler graph and temporary physical files only; actual source-owner composition not run

test_coverage_gaps_and_nonclaims: The controls use synthetic nodes/readers and a temporary two-file model; they do not prove actual WeakMap brands, 70→69→68 frame projections, callback-free real physical preflight/final, legacy population or exact M3 absent paths.

Graph mutation tests cover function replacement and accessor/proxy/sparse/cycle rejection, but do not separately demonstrate root-array/dependency-array replacement, post-capture accessor installation, or descriptor-flag mutation during a callback; add targeted cases if these guarantees are relied on.

Receiver test confirms this is undefined in an ES-module strict function; a sloppy-mode function gets globalThis rather than undefined, which still must never be the internal snapshot. Consider a Function-created sloppy callback test.

Direct returned thenable and Promise.resolve are covered; rejected Promise behavior and a predicate that schedules later work but returns undefined are not covered. Rejecting every source of delayed side effect is not possible through function type checks alone; genuine owner adapters must be synchronous by construction.

The 13 controls establish neither provenance of actual owner predicates nor completeness of their source/absence/population/captured-metadata checks. Preserve and run the earlier compound lifetime review and original full cold/late CLI paths after real integration.
Internal callback ordering/count is not a compatibility API; tests may verify scheduler’s declared phase order but must not demand former recursive counts or cache real owner judgments.
